bare.rule: Start with the ball in the middle and a hidden orientation in normal mode. Shake toggles the hidden orientation and does not move the ball. In normal mode, tilt left moves the ball one slot left and tilt right moves it one slot right. In flipped mode, those directions reverse. The ball stays at an end if it cannot move further.

rounds.rule: Start at middle in a normal orientation: tilt left/right rolls the ball one slot in that named direction, saturating at edges; shake leaves the ball where it is but toggles to a reversed orientation, in which tilt left/right rolls the ball the opposite way.

commitments.why: If this ended left or middle, the shake did not flip the direction of subsequent tilts as the rule requires.
If this ended right or middle, the shake did not flip the direction of subsequent tilts as the rule requires.
If this ended left or middle, shake does not invert tilt-left into a rightward roll.
If this ended right or middle, shake does not invert tilt-right into a leftward roll.
If this ended left, the intervening shake did not flip the tilt direction; if right, the first tilt or edge saturation is wrong.

rounds.rule: Start at middle with a hidden orientation set to normal. A tilt moves the ball one slot in its named direction when the orientation is normal, or one slot in the opposite direction when the orientation is flipped, stopping at left/right; a shake flips the hidden orientation but does not move the ball.

commitments.why: The shake flips the hidden orientation, so the final tilt left must act like a tilt right and move the ball to right; any other result would refute the orientation-flip rule.
After the initial shake, left/right tilts are reversed; this sequence should move right, then left, then right again, so a different final state would contradict the hidden-flip model.
One shake makes tilt left move the ball rightward, and once at right further reversed left-tilts should leave it clamped there; a different result would disprove the flip plus boundary rule.
Two shakes cancel the orientation flip, so the final tilt left should move the ball from right back to middle; otherwise the parity effect of shakes is wrong.
Two left tilts clamp the ball at left, and two shakes should flip the orientation twice without moving it, so it must remain left; a different result would mean shakes move the ball or do not cancel.

attack, rebuild fresh.final_rule: Start at middle with a hidden reversed flag false. Shake toggles the flag. Tilt left moves the ball one place left if the flag is false, or one place right if the flag is true. Tilt right moves the ball one place right if the flag is false, or one place left if the flag is true. The ball stops at the left/right boundaries.

rounds.rule: The ball starts in the middle with a hidden mode that is normal. Shaking toggles the hidden mode without moving the ball; in normal mode tilt-left moves one slot left and tilt-right one slot right, while in reversed mode those directions are swapped, with the ball stopping at the ends.

commitments.why: An odd shake puts the hidden mode in reversed, so two left tilts push to the right edge and the right tilt brings it back to middle; another outcome would falsify the swap rule.
Odd shake leaves reversed mode; left then right then left should push right, then back to middle, then right again, so any other result would doubt the reversed-direction rule.
The shake flips to reversed mode at the left edge, where tilt-right should move or stay left, so a different result would cast doubt on the edge behavior in reversed mode.
The shake flips to reversed mode at the right edge; tilt-right then tilt-left should return to right, so if it does not the reversal-at-edge rule is wrong.
Odd shake means reversed mode; right moves left, left moves right, and right moves left again to end left, so a different result would falsify the toggle-and-reversal rule.

rounds.rule: The ball starts in the middle with a hidden mode set to normal. Shaking flips the hidden mode; in normal mode tilt-left moves the ball left and tilt-right moves it right, while in flipped mode those directions are swapped, and tilting outward at an edge leaves the ball at that edge.

commitments.why: Three shakes should put the hidden mode in flipped, so tilt-left from the middle must move right; if it ends left or middle, the hidden-mode toggle or reversed direction is wrong.
After one shake, the directions should be swapped, so right then left then left should end right; any other final state would cast doubt on the reversal rule.
After one shake, left moves right, then right moves left twice, so the ball should finish left; a different result would falsify the swapped-direction behavior.
The ball starts left, shaking flips the mode, then left moves it right and right moves it left, so it should return to left; otherwise the shake-toggle rule is likely wrong.
At the right edge in flipped mode, tilt-left should leave it at right, then tilt-right should move it to middle; if not, the edge-clamping or flipped-direction rule is suspect.

attack, defend.final_rule: The ball starts in the middle in a normal hidden mode. Shaking toggles the hidden mode; in normal mode tilt-left moves the ball left and tilt-right moves it right, while in reversed mode those directions are swapped, and tilting outward at an edge leaves the ball at that edge.
